gloss: doing things like…; sometimes … and sometimes …

definitions.explanation: Attached to the た-form of a verb or adjective to list a few actions or states as examples among others, in the pattern 〜たり〜たりする. The last たり is followed by する (or です/だ after the list). Unlike the て-form, it does not say the actions happen in that order or that the list is complete.

With opposite or contrasting verbs, 〜たり〜たり describes something that keeps going back and forth: rain that starts and stops, a person who comes and goes. A single 〜たりする is also used to soften a statement, offering one action as an example ("things like…").

examples.japanese: ⟦{週末|しゅうまつ}→週末：03030_shuumatsu⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{本|ほん}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{読|よ}ん→読む：00426_yomu⟧だり⟦します→する：00392_suru⟧。
examples.english: On weekends I do things like reading.

examples.japanese: ⟦{休|やす}み→休み：02266_yasumi⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{日|ひ}→日：02249_hi⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{掃除|そうじ}→掃除：02889_souji⟧したり⟦{洗濯|せんたく}→洗濯：13283_sentaku⟧したり⟦する→する：00392_suru⟧。
examples.english: On my days off I clean, do laundry, and so on.

examples.japanese: ⟦{昨日|きのう}→昨日：00859_kinou⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{友達|ともだち}→友達：01478_tomodachi⟧⟦と→と：00512_to⟧⟦{映画|えいが}→映画：02273_eiga⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{見|み}→見る：00283_miru⟧たり、⟦{買|か}い{物|もの}→買い物：00853_kaimono⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧したり⟦して→する：00392_suru⟧⟦{楽|たの}しかった→楽しい：00817_tanoshii⟧。
examples.english: Yesterday I had fun seeing a movie, shopping, and so on with a friend.

examples.japanese: ⟦{雨|あめ}→雨：00583_ame⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{降|ふ}っ→降る：00839_furu⟧たり⟦{止|や}ん→止む：01153_yamu⟧だり⟦している→する：00392_suru⟧。
examples.english: It keeps raining on and off.
He was pacing back and forth in the room.

examples.japanese: ⟦この→この：00962_kono⟧⟦{時期|じき}→時期：03269_jiki⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{暑|あつ}かっ→暑い：00619_atsui⟧たり⟦{寒|さむ}かっ→寒い：00664_samui⟧たり⟦する→する：00392_suru⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧で、⟦{服|ふく}→服：00695_fuku⟧{選|えら}び⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{難|むずか}しい→難しい：00517_muzukashii⟧。
examples.english: This time of year it's hot one day and cold the next, so it's hard to choose what to wear.

notes:
FORMS:
- Verbs: た-form + り — ⟦{食|た}べ→食べる：00396_taberu⟧たり, ⟦{読|よ}ん→読む：00426_yomu⟧だり (the だ of a voiced た-form carries over)
- i-adjectives: ⟦{高|たか}かっ→高い：00500_takai⟧たり, ⟦{安|やす}かっ→安い：00464_yasui⟧たり
- Nouns and na-adjectives: ⟦{雨|あめ}→雨：00583_ame⟧だったり, ⟦{静|しず}か→静か：00755_shizuka⟧だったり
- Negative: ⟦{行|い}かなかっ→行く：00119_iku⟧たり

COMMON PATTERNS:
- 〜たり〜たり⟦する→する：00392_suru⟧: do things like A and B
- ⟦{行|い}っ→行く：00119_iku⟧たり{来|き}たり: back and forth
- ⟦{降|ふ}っ→降る：00839_furu⟧たり⟦{止|や}ん→止む：01153_yamu⟧だり: raining on and off
- 〜たり⟦しないで→する：00392_suru⟧: please don't do something like…

WATCH OUT:
In careful speech and writing every listed verb takes たり, including the last: ⟦{見|み}→見る：00283_miru⟧たり⟦{聞|き}い→聞く：00483_kiku⟧たり⟦する→する：00392_suru⟧, not ⟦{見|み}→見る：00283_miru⟧たり⟦{聞|き}く→聞く：00483_kiku⟧. Casual speech often drops the second たり.

SIMILAR WORDS:
- て-form: links actions or states; with successive actions it usually gives their order, and it does not suggest "among other things"
- し: lists facts or reasons, often in support of a conclusion; it can list activities too, but does not need ⟦する→する：00392_suru⟧ at the end
- ⟦と→と：00512_to⟧⟦か→か：09473_ka⟧: lists examples of things or actions, more casual
